newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds broadly unchanged, good two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds broadly unchanged, good two-way trade.

text.p: Irish bonds were broadly unchanged on Tuesday in the absence of market-moving data, although dealers reported good two-way trade.

"Unlike other markets today we've seen moderate to good volume within a narrow range," one dealer said. "There's been very little price action and at the longer end bonds are pretty much unchanged, but that's to be expected when there's a dearth of news to give direction."

Thin volume has been a feature of direction-hungry world bond markets over the last few days with trade unlikely to improve until the run up to significant U.S. data employment and GDP data next week.

In the meantime the market will be looking at the release of March UK retail sales data swiftly followed by a 2.0 billion pounds sterling auction by the Bank of England of seven percent gilts stock due 2002 on Wednesday.
Irish final retail sales figures for January and provisional figures for February are due on Friday.

On the Irish market at 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 13.5 pence from Monday's close at 101.94 to yield 5.98 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 gained eight pence to 108.33 to yield 6.76 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 145 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area, and 89 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area - one tick back apiece from Monday.
